description: Single source of truth for research suites, batches, studies, inputs, and dependencies. Generated prompts and manifests must derive from this file.

studies.title: Architecture validation
Language and stack selection
Security and privacy
Windows feasibility
Scale and reliability
Requirements and migration

batches.title: Immediate pre-implementation foundations
batches.timing: Run first. Prompts 01–06 may run in parallel, then run the batch reviewer.
batches.cli: Profile evidence; prepare decision/ADR templates; prepare the Windows lab without connecting; create fictional identity seeds; establish repository quality gates. Do not implement G1 security details until prompt 02 is reviewed.
batches.gate: Accept the G0 data contract, G1 blueprint, contract rules, application identity model, privacy ceiling, and repository boundaries before production-shaped endpoint code.

batches.title: Endpoint source and privacy transformation
batches.timing: May run while G1 is implemented. Prompts 07–08 may run in parallel after the Batch 1 accepted baseline is available.
batches.cli: Implement and test G1; create synthetic Edge profiles and localhost fixtures; build a canary corpus; collect no real activity data.
batches.gate: G1 must pass before integrating live source acquisition. G2/G3 and G4 must pass before any source value enters the production outbox.

batches.title: Durability, testing, release, identity, diagnostics, and compatibility
batches.timing: May run while G2–G5 prototypes are built. Prompts 09–14 can run in parallel but must consume accepted Batch 1–2 decisions.
batches.cli: Finish source/privacy prototypes; prepare crash, reboot, disk-pressure, certificate, proxy, package-tamper, and compatibility harnesses; keep production credentials and data out.
batches.gate: Outbox invariants, update authorization, device identity, privacy-safe support, and the initial supported-platform claim must pass before an engineering canary.

batches.title: Server ingestion, database, capacity, and data lifecycle
batches.timing: Run after endpoint contracts are stable enough to simulate. Prompts 15–18 may run in parallel; database choice remains measurement-gated.
batches.cli: Build a contract-accurate endpoint simulator; prepare isolated PostgreSQL and SQL Server candidates; implement synthetic poison/replay workloads; gather metadata-only distributions when approved.
batches.gate: Durable receipt/idempotency must pass before endpoint deletion after ACK. Database, capacity, retention, RPO/RTO, and broker decisions require measured evidence and human approval.

batches.title: Portal authorization, workflows, and audit
batches.timing: Run once control-plane concepts and data classifications are stable. Prompts 19–21 may run in parallel.
batches.cli: Prepare API authorization test scaffolding, synthetic personas, accessibility tooling, and audit fixtures; do not encode final roles before owners approve them.
batches.gate: Capability authorization, purpose-bound access, transactional audit, accessibility, and break-glass controls must pass before administrative production use.

batches.title: Legacy discovery, parallel validation, cutover, and decommissioning
batches.timing: Run after the new contracts and first vertical slice are understood. Prompts 22–24 may run in parallel, then reconcile them.
batches.cli: Inventory consumers and credentials read-only; build comparison digests with synthetic fixtures; monitor legacy paths; never execute deferred legacy SQL or disable production paths during research.
batches.gate: Named owners must approve every consumer/configuration disposition, reconciliation result, rollback boundary, credential removal, and final decommission action.

studies.title: G0 dummy-data and test-oracle architecture
studies.role: principal test-data architect, privacy engineer, and model-based testing lead
questions: Define three safe data tiers: fully fictional committed fixtures, sanitized organization-shaped internal data, and tightly controlled measured evidence.
Design canonical synthetic organization, role, persona, account, device, session, application, policy, event, batch, receipt, audit, deletion, migration, and expected-result models.

Define deterministic seeds, clocks, identifiers, distributions, scenario composition, data lineage, schema evolution, and a truth ledger that predicts accepted/rejected/quarantined outcomes and cursor progress.
Map datasets to G1–G12, including privacy canaries, cross-session attacks, browser locks, duplicates, outages, disk pressure, restore, and 6,000-device load.
Specify how the sanitized catalogue profile informs shape without copying internal values or inventing role mappings.
deliverables: Logical and physical dummy-data schemas with example fictional records
Dataset catalogue by proof gate, size, classification, retention, and owner
human: Whether any real application names may be used internally
cli: Implement generator and schema after review
Run canary scans and scenario reconciliation
studies.gate: No production-shaped fixture or live pilot data exists without classification, provenance, expected result, owner, and deletion method.

studies.title: G1 Windows Coordinator, User Host, Task Host, session identity, and IPC blueprint
studies.role: principal Windows security engineer and .NET endpoint architect
questions: Specify the Coordinator Service, per-interactive-session User Host, and restricted Task Host processes down to executable ownership, lifecycle, startup, shutdown, recovery, and dependency rules.

Choose and justify service identity, service SID, privileges, filesystem/registry/certificate ACLs, Scheduled Task principal/logon/run-level/triggers, and behavior for console, lock, fast switch, RDP, disconnect, logoff, and same-SID sessions.

Define named-pipe or alternative IPC namespace, ACL construction, local-only enforcement, handshake, nonce, framing, version negotiation, caller token/SID/logon-SID/session/PID/creation-time validation, replay/PID-reuse defenses, cancellation, quotas, timeouts, malformed clients, and DoS containment.
Define Task Host token restriction, Job Object rules, inherited handles, network prohibition, filesystem capabilities, mitigations, kill-tree behavior, and residual limitations.
Produce a code-ready .NET solution blueprint and exact G1 hostile test plan without connecting to the lab.
deliverables: Exact component/project responsibilities and allowed dependencies
IPC wire protocol and state machine with example messages
G1 test harness specification with commands, evidence, pass/fail, cleanup
human: Enterprise Scheduled Task and service policy constraints
Acceptable resource budget and support model
cli: Implement the smallest LocalService/User Host/hostile-client proof
studies.gate: Zero cross-session accepted messages; no profile access by the service; no prohibited privileges; bounded hostile-client impact.
oss: Windows Service plus per-user agent implementations
Windows Job Object and restricted-token sandboxes

studies.title: Contract, compatibility, and versioning strategy
studies.role: principal protocol architect and compatibility engineer
questions: Define contract families for collector invocation/result, privacy transformation, IPC, policy/privacy ceiling, local events, batches, receipts, quarantine, health, audit, integration, and deletion tombstones.

Specify canonical serialization, schema identifiers, field presence/nullability, numeric/time/identifier rules, maximum sizes, unknown/duplicate field behavior, strictness, hashes/signatures, and test vectors.

Define backward/forward compatibility, supported-version windows, producer/consumer rollout order, N/N-1 or broader rules, deprecation, reservation, rollback, unsupported-schema behavior, and compatibility observability.
Prevent shared DTOs from coupling endpoint persistence, server storage, portal views, and external integrations.
Decide what needs a formal specification versus OpenAPI/JSON Schema/code generation, while leaving binary encoding measurement-gated.
deliverables: Example schemas/messages and canonical test vectors
Contract test strategy and architecture fitness functions
cli: Implement schema linting and golden vectors
Measure JSON/gzip before considering another encoding
studies.gate: No component integration begins without a versioned contract, owner, size limits, compatibility rule, and rejection behavior.

studies.title: Application registry, aliases, ownership, and URL/process matching
studies.role: enterprise application-data architect and rule-engine designer
questions: Design UAM-owned stable application identity, nullable/non-authoritative external keys, aliases, source provenance, lifecycle, ownership, sensitivity, categories, and CMDB links.

Design revisioned URL/domain and process/publisher/product/path rules with normalization versions, priority, specificity, effective dates, conflicts, shadowing, testing, approvals, rollback, and endpoint snapshot publication.
Define unknown/unmatched/ambiguous behavior and prohibit deriving real rules from names alone.
Define import staging and quality workflow for missing/duplicate external IDs and unsafe/truncated labels without exposing catalogue values.
Define rule simulation, impact preview, fixture generation, conflict detection, data lineage, and realm isolation.
deliverables: Endpoint snapshot contract and size strategy
Test matrix with fictional URL/process examples
human: Application owners and source of truth
Who may create, approve, publish, and retire rules
studies.gate: No real rule is published without owner, purpose, revision, test examples, conflict result, approval, and rollback.

studies.title: Product privacy ceiling and tenant-policy narrowing
studies.role: privacy-by-design architect and policy security engineer
questions: Define a release-authorized product privacy ceiling covering sources, fields, transformations, capabilities, destinations, diagnostic levels, and hard-deny classes.

Define typed signed tenant policy that may only narrow the ceiling, including scope, targeting, effective/expiry, revision, approval, rollback, offline cache, kill switches, invalid/unknown/expired behavior, and old-agent compatibility.
Specify where enforcement occurs in Task Host, User Host, Coordinator, server, portal, and release pipeline, and how no single compromised plane can broaden collection.
Define policy ownership, configuration provenance, feature flags, emergency disablement, policy simulation, impact preview, audit, and safe recovery.
Provide formalizable invariants and negative tests proving policy monotonicity.
deliverables: Ceiling and tenant-policy schemas with fictional examples
Policy evaluation and rollout state machines
human: Approved purposes, fields, sources, hard-deny categories, and identity/time precision
cli: Scan all sinks for forbidden canaries
studies.gate: Invalid, expired, unsupported, or broader policy produces zero new collection and an audited, privacy-safe health state.

studies.title: Repository, solution, build, dependency, and CI architecture
studies.role: principal build/release engineer and secure software architect
questions: Design the repository and .NET/frontend/tooling solution layout, project boundaries, dependency direction, shared-code limits, test layers, generated artifacts, configuration ownership, and architecture fitness functions.

Define reproducible builds, locked dependencies, analyzers, formatting, test isolation, secret scanning, license policy, SBOM, provenance, artifact naming, versioning, signing handoff, promotion, and branch protections.
Define Windows-specific CI needs, safe test certificates, emulator versus real-VM lanes, cache poisoning defenses, fork/PR trust, runner isolation, and least-privilege credentials.
Define secure coding/review standards, threat-model updates, dependency exception workflow, patch SLAs, and evidence retention.
Keep exact vendor/tool versions provisional and specify selection/update policies instead.
deliverables: Repository tree and project dependency diagram
CI/CD lane design and trust boundaries
cli: Prove clean reproducible build and SBOM generation
studies.gate: No production artifact is promoted without reproducible inputs, review evidence, dependency/license checks, provenance, and separated signing authority.

studies.title: G2/G3 Edge profile discovery, safe acquisition, source identity, and cursor correctness
studies.role: senior Windows browser-storage engineer and data-correctness specialist
questions: Specify supported Edge profile discovery, policy-defined roots, multi-profile handling, source IDs, source generations, same-SID concurrent sessions, profile removal/recreation, and unsupported/custom roots.
Compare short read-only transactions, SQLite Online Backup, and defer behavior under live writes and locks; define scratch ACLs, lifecycle, cancellation, cleanup, and proof of zero source writes.
Define schema capability detection and current/previous-version fixture strategy without treating browser internals as a stable public API.

Define native visit-ID/source-time cursor, bounded overlap, late synchronization, same timestamps, deletions, ID reuse/regression, DB replacement, clock/DST/sleep behavior, checkpoint atomicity, and deterministic dedupe input.
Specify the smallest G2/G3 VM prototypes and browser-impact measurements.
deliverables: Exact G2/G3 implementation backlog and pass/fail tests
human: Supported Edge channels/versions and profile technologies
First-run lookback and allowed time precision
cli: Create synthetic profiles and localhost visits
Use filesystem tracing to prove zero writes
studies.gate: Failed/busy/unsupported/corrupt reads never advance; controlled fixture recall is complete; no cross-profile/session mix or source writes.

studies.title: G4 URL canonicalization, application matching, and endpoint privacy transformation
studies.role: URL standards expert, application-security engineer, and privacy transformation architect
questions: Define parsing/canonicalization order for schemes, hosts, IDNA/Unicode, case, trailing dots, ports, userinfo, percent encoding, paths, queries, fragments, control characters, invalid input, and public-suffix considerations.
Define endpoint allowlisting/site mapping and application-rule evaluation using accepted registry contracts, including ambiguity and versioned normalization.
Specify hard-deny detection, field minimization, time/identity reduction, rejected-value telemetry that never logs the value, and final privacy boundary placement.
Design a differential/property/fuzz test corpus covering encoding tricks, sensitive canaries, very large input, parser disagreement, and rule conflicts.
State when a custom implementation is too risky and which maintained libraries are suitable after license/security review.
cli: Implement golden vectors before production logic
studies.gate: No forbidden source value or reversible derivative crosses into Coordinator IPC, durable storage, diagnostics, or transport.

studies.title: G5 SQLite outbox, batching, receipts, encryption, migrations, and state machines
studies.role: database reliability engineer and distributed state-machine architect
questions: Design the one-writer SQLite schema for sources/generations/cursors, events, batches, attempts, receipts, runs, policies, health, encryption metadata, migrations, quarantine, and cleanup.

Define event-plus-cursor transaction, stable identity/dedupe, sequence, batch construction, immutable content hash, send/lost-response/receipt/replay transitions, grace retention, and terminal states.

Specify WAL/FULL/checkpoint/busy/foreign-key/trusted-schema/integrity settings, connection ownership, shutdown, antivirus interference, corruption, disk-full/free-space reserve, quotas, priority/pause, and no-silent-loss rules.
Evaluate payload encryption, CNG/DPAPI/TPM wrapping, rotation, recovery, metadata leakage, and local-admin residual risk.
Define expand/contract migrations, N/N-1 rollback, backup/repair/quarantine, observability, and formal invariants.
human: Maximum offline duration and pause/loss policy
Local data sensitivity and encryption assurance
Endpoint disk budget and ACK grace tied to RPO
cli: Measure WAL, latency, memory, and recovery
studies.gate: No cursor-ahead state, missing committed event, silent unacknowledged deletion, or duplicate final effect under fault injection.

studies.title: Model-based, property-based, fault-injection, and invariant testing
studies.role: principal verification engineer and reliability test architect
questions: Create a unified verification strategy for session isolation, privacy monotonicity, source cursor correctness, SQLite durability, idempotent receipts/materialization, update rollback, realm isolation, deletion/restore, and audit atomicity.

Choose model-based/property/fuzz/concurrency/fault tools for C#/.NET, Windows, SQLite, HTTP, and relational databases; define deterministic seeds, virtual clocks, shrink/replay, evidence, and CI versus lab lanes.
Specify injectable fault points at OS/process/file/transaction/network/worker/restore boundaries and avoid tests that only mock away the failure.
Define architecture fitness functions and release gates, including flaky-test policy and coverage limits.
Search open source for mature frameworks and real failure-injection examples, assessing maintenance and licenses.
deliverables: Reproducible evidence format and ordered harness backlog
human: Required evidence depth and release blocking policy
cli: Store minimized failing seeds and evidence
studies.gate: Every load-bearing invariant has an automated falsification path or an explicitly owned manual exercise.

studies.title: MSI, enterprise deployment, updater, rollback, signing, TUF-style metadata, and supply chain
studies.role: Windows release-security architect and software supply-chain engineer
questions: Separate MSI/enterprise-management ownership from any optional autonomous updater; define when self-update is justified by measured patch latency.

Specify installation/repair/uninstall, stable launcher, immutable version directories, staging, hashes/lengths, Authenticode, repository metadata roles/expiry/thresholds, key rotation/revocation/recovery, freeze/rollback/mix-and-match protection, A/B activation, health proof, bad-version suppression, emergency downgrade, and N/N-1 data compatibility.
Threat-model SYSTEM file operations, reparse/TOCTOU, ACL inheritance, service/task changes, untrusted repository responses, compromised CI/signing keys, and offline devices.
Define SBOM/provenance/reproducibility, isolated signing, promotion rings, kill switches, incident response, and out-of-band repair.
Compare maintained TUF/updater/MSI open-source references without assuming direct dependency suitability.
deliverables: Enterprise deployment versus updater decision gate
human: Patch SLA and enterprise management coverage
cli: Prove MSI repair and rollback without production keys
studies.gate: Unauthorized or incomplete versions never execute; every interruption leaves an operable known version; key compromise has a tested recovery path.

studies.title: Device enrollment, certificates, TPM, cloning, revocation, proxy, VPN, and realm identity
studies.role: enterprise PKI architect and zero-trust device identity engineer
questions: Design bootstrap enrollment, per-installation identity, device certificate/key lifecycle, TPM-backed and software fallback assurance, renewal, revocation, rapid denylisting, re-enrollment, clock skew, lost/offline devices, and support diagnostics.
Define golden-image/clone/nonpersistent VDI handling, enrollment epochs, duplicate identity detection, realm mapping, decommission, and ownership transfer.
Compare mTLS termination/pass-through, certificate-bound tokens if useful, proxy/VPN/TLS inspection behavior, gateway trust, header stripping, and no-shared-fleet-secret fallback.
Define server-derived realm/device authority and prevent body/header/cache/store confusion across every plane.
Produce lab and customer-network compatibility tests rather than asserting universal TPM/proxy support.
cli: Use a lab CA and synthetic identities
Never export private keys into evidence
studies.gate: Cloned, revoked, expired, unknown, or wrong-realm identities fail closed without a shared secret workaround.

studies.title: Privacy-safe diagnostics, logging, support bundles, and temporary diagnostic access
studies.role: observability architect, privacy engineer, and enterprise support lead
questions: Define endpoint/server/portal structured log and error taxonomies with bounded fields, correlation, fingerprints, severity, retryability, owner, user-safe messages, and no raw activity values.
Define OpenTelemetry metrics/traces and label-cardinality limits, sampling, propagation, storage, redaction, exception handling, crash behavior, and safe access logging.

Design support bundles using hashes/counts/status/configuration versions only, deterministic collection, size limits, consent/authorization, encryption, expiry, upload, access, deletion, and canary scanning.
Design temporary diagnostics policy with purpose/ticket/target/level/approval/expiry/kill switch and prevent it from exceeding the privacy ceiling.
Define incident response, runbooks, L1/L2/L3 ownership, supportability tests, and residual blind spots.
deliverables: Error taxonomy and structured event schemas
cli: Seed canaries through all failure paths
studies.gate: Support can diagnose defined failures without raw URLs, paths, identities, secrets, or unbounded telemetry.

studies.title: Windows, browser, RDP/RDS, profile, ARM64, EDR, sleep, and compatibility policy
studies.role: Windows enterprise compatibility lead and browser platform engineer
questions: Define supported/conditional/test-only/unsupported matrices for Windows editions/releases/LTSC/Server, x64/ARM64, Edge/Chrome/Firefox channels, console/RDP/RDS/AVD, FSLogix/Citrix/roaming profiles, multi-session/same-SID, sleep/hibernate/Modern Standby, proxies/VPNs, Defender and third-party EDR.

Define qualification cadence, browser schema fixtures, OS servicing, runtime packaging, dependency native-architecture checks, EDR exclusions policy, support expiry, health reporting, and fail-closed behavior.
Separate VM-provable claims from physical hardware and enterprise-environment claims.
Specify compatibility test lanes, representative matrices, evidence, exception/waiver lifecycle, and customer readiness questionnaires.
Avoid claiming support from vendor documentation alone.
cli: Record unsupported states without silent success
studies.gate: No platform is labeled supported until its security, acquisition, update, durability, resource, and cleanup gates pass.

studies.title: Ingestion API, durable relational inbox, idempotency, leasing, quarantine, and materialization
studies.role: principal distributed-systems and relational ingestion architect
questions: Define gateway/API trust boundaries, mTLS-derived identity, header stripping, streaming compressed/decompressed limits, canonical batch hash, cheap synchronous validation, durable receipt semantics, duplicate same/different hash behavior, and receipt lookup.

Design engine-neutral relational inbox, immutable payload custody, worker leases/heartbeats, retries, poison/unsupported schema quarantine, event dedupe, materialization, aggregate projection, reconciliation, and terminal states.
Define transaction/failure boundaries for process/host/DB failover, lost responses, worker death after fact insert, replay after restore, backpressure, fairness, and realm isolation.
Specify schemas, indexes, state machines, observability/error taxonomy, operational tools, retention links, and integration outbox boundaries.
Evaluate external broker only against explicit measured break-even requirements.
deliverables: Worker lease and batch state machines
cli: Implement contract emulator and poison corpus
studies.gate: Every durable receipt remains recoverable and reaches one materialized effect or explicit terminal quarantine.

studies.title: PostgreSQL versus SQL Server experimental comparison
studies.role: independent database performance, operations, and cost evaluator
questions: Design a fair, engine-neutral experiment using identical semantic schemas, data, ingest/materialization logic, indexes, query corpus, retention, late arrivals, restore, failover, backup, observability, and hardware/service class.

Compare durable inbox leasing, bulk ingestion, dedupe/uniqueness with partitioning, WAL/log amplification, vacuum/index maintenance, partition operations, report coexistence, HA/DR, security/realm isolation, tooling, skills, licensing, managed/on-prem options, and on-call burden.
Define benchmark anti-patterns, warmup, repetitions, confidence intervals, reproducibility, cost normalization, and decision weighting/sensitivity.
Keep exact product versions current at execution and pin them in evidence rather than the architecture baseline.
Produce a decision gate, not a predetermined winner.
cli: Run both candidates with identical generated data
studies.gate: Database ADR requires production-shaped results, restore/failover evidence, skills/TCO assessment, and owner approval.

studies.title: Capacity model, 6,000-device simulator, reconnect storms, recovery, and broker break-even
studies.role: capacity planner and distributed reliability engineer
questions: Define replaceable variables and formulas for active endpoints, users/sessions, events, bytes, compression, batches, retries, outages, local/central backlog, drain rate, storage/index/WAL, retention, queries, and cost.
Design a stateful 6,000–12,000-device simulator using production contracts/serializer/compression/IDs/retry/receipts, plus open-arrival API load and a Windows fidelity cohort.
Specify steady, morning, reconnect, site outage, multi-day backlog, policy fanout, poison, slow DB, restore, and rolling-update traffic shapes with deterministic seeds and fairness.
Define SLIs/SLO hypotheses, recovery equations, headroom, soak, dashboards, cardinality, alert/runbook ownership, and metadata-only measurements needed from legacy/pilot.
Define quantitative external-broker break-even conditions and avoid sizing from endpoint count alone.
studies.gate: Capacity choices require measured tails and recovery tests with agreed headroom; a broker is added only after a stated trigger is crossed.

studies.title: Retention, deletion, backup, restore, tombstones, exports, and integration deletion
studies.role: data lifecycle architect, privacy engineer, and disaster-recovery specialist
questions: Map lifecycle across endpoint outbox/grace, gateway/inbox/quarantine, facts/aggregates, caches, replicas, search, logs, audit, exports, integrations, backups, restored environments, and legal holds.

Design purpose/field-based retention policy representation, deletion requests, subject resolution, tombstone ledger, connector/export registry, retry/evidence, backup expiry, restore-time re-deletion, read-readiness gates, and acknowledged-event replay.
Reconcile immutable audit/evidence with erasure, minimize raw retention, and define cryptographic deletion/key-boundary limits.
Define failure/incident behavior for partial deletion, unavailable destination, restore before tombstones, stale caches, recipient copies, and accidental reingestion.
Separate technical mechanisms from human/legal retention decisions.
human: Purpose, legal basis, retention, legal hold, rights process
cli: Delete, restore older backup, replay tombstones and endpoint grace
studies.gate: A restored environment exposes neither missing acknowledged events nor deleted fictional subjects before it is declared ready.

studies.title: Portal capability model, RBAC/ABAC, JIT access, approvals, and break-glass
studies.role: enterprise IAM authorization architect and privacy access-control engineer
questions: Define resources/actions/scopes/realms/purposes/conditions for fleet, policy, applications/rules, detail, aggregates, diagnostics, exports, tasks, releases, deletion, audit, and integrations.

Design capability RBAC plus limited ABAC, deny-by-default API enforcement, tenant isolation, separation of duties, JIT grants, approvals, purpose/ticket/target/time, break-glass, expiry/revocation, delegated administration, and service identities.
Define OIDC/BFF session/token/CSRF boundaries, authorization decision logging without sensitive payloads, caching invalidation, outage behavior, and emergency lockout recovery.
Specify positive/negative/property tests for every route/mutation and cross-realm confused-deputy cases.
Do not infer organization roles; provide a mapping workshop and safe provisional personas.
deliverables: Authorization policy model and decision flow
cli: Implement server-side negative tests before UI
studies.gate: Every API action is denied unless an explicit capability, realm, purpose, and condition permits it; cross-realm access tests are zero-tolerance.

studies.title: Portal information architecture and administrative workflows
studies.role: enterprise product designer, accessibility specialist, and operations workflow architect
questions: Design information architecture and task flows for fleet health, population/policy, application registry/rules/conflicts, task/release rollout, aggregates/detail, diagnostics/errors, audit, exports/deletion, integrations, and support.

Apply aggregate-first and least-detail defaults, impact preview, reason/approval, optimistic concurrency, draft/review/publish/rollback, staged rollout, kill switches, bulk-action safety, empty/error/stale/offline states, and safe recovery.

Define workflow ownership, status/state models, notification/escalation, accessibility to current WCAG/enterprise standards, localization/time zones, keyboard/screen-reader support, and performance budgets.
Separate browser UI from API authority; no generic direct table editor or hidden production actions.
Specify usability/accessibility tests with synthetic data and representative roles.
deliverables: Phased portal backlog and acceptance criteria
human: Whether any detail view is needed
studies.gate: Normal administration is possible without direct DB access, generic row mutation, inaccessible controls, or unaudited high-risk action.

studies.title: Transactional audit, tamper evidence, external verification, and audit access
studies.role: security audit architect and forensic integrity engineer
questions: Define typed audit events for authentication/authorization, reads of sensitive detail, exports, policy/rule/task/release changes, diagnostics, approvals, break-glass, deletion, integration, and failures.

Design mutation-plus-audit atomicity, event schema, actor/service/realm/capability/purpose/target/diff/result/correlation/time, sequencing, hash chaining or ledger alternatives, external digests/verification, key custody, and ordinary-admin non-deletion.
Define audit access, search, retention, redaction, subject-data minimization, export, alerting, daily verification, gap handling, DB restore/replay, and incident response.
Compare engine-native and external tamper-evidence options through threat model, operations, licensing, and verification independence.
Specify tests for omitted/duplicated/reordered/altered events and unavailable audit sinks.
studies.gate: A privileged mutation cannot succeed without durable audit, and ordinary product/database administration cannot alter history undetected.

studies.title: Legacy consumer, report, script, schedule, credential, buffer, and integration discovery
studies.role: legacy modernization discovery lead and database dependency analyst
questions: Design a read-only discovery method for endpoint versions/settings/checkpoints/buffers, DB objects/logins/jobs/queries/reports, PSU routes/actions, scripts/schedules, HR/AD joins, exports, integrations, firewall paths, service accounts, manual workflows, and unreachable devices.

Define evidence/provenance, owner interviews, static and runtime observation, false-negative limits, dynamic SQL/ad-hoc consumer treatment, sensitivity-safe output, and how to prove absence over time.
Create a disposition model: preserve approved outcome, deliberately change, retire, investigate/quarantine; never execute deferred SQL or scripts during discovery.
Define credential/buffer classification and incident handling without copying secrets or raw activity.
Specify a traceability graph from legacy evidence to requirement, consumer, new component, test, migration, rollback, owner, and removal proof.
cli: Observe residual use over an agreed window
studies.gate: No legacy behavior, data, credential, script, or consumer is migrated or removed without evidence, owner, disposition, validation, and rollback.

studies.title: Parallel-run comparison, reconciliation, compatibility projection, and migration validation
studies.role: data migration validation architect and statistical reconciliation lead
questions: Define one-authoritative-writer architecture, server-side compatibility projection, shadow data paths, and prohibition of endpoint dual-write.

Define exact invariants versus approved tolerances for counts, source ranges, keyed digests, timestamps/buckets, rule outcomes, checkpoints, aggregates, errors, and reports while minimizing sensitive detail duplication.

Design canonical comparison keys, known-defect register, mismatch taxonomy, sampling/break-glass, provenance, late data, retries, dedupe differences, timezone/identity differences, owner review, and automated pause/rollback thresholds.
Define configuration transformation validation and historical/read-only strategy.
Specify migration evidence and sign-off without treating legacy output as automatically correct.
cli: Use synthetic and approved aggregate fixtures
studies.gate: Every exact invariant passes; every tolerated mismatch has an owner-approved reason; endpoint dual-write remains impossible.

studies.title: Cutover, rollback, legacy read-only operation, credential removal, monitoring, and decommissioning
studies.role: enterprise cutover director, security engineer, and operational readiness lead
questions: Design staged canary/ring cutover, authority transfer, bake periods, automated pause, smallest-safe rollback unit, full rollback conditions, data/schema compatibility, and communications/on-call/change control.

Define legacy portal read-only transition, compatibility write expiry, historical archive access, endpoint buffer disposition, unreachable devices, schedule/script disablement, database login/certificate/secret revocation, network denial, service account/firewall/CMDB cleanup, and residual activity monitoring.
Define runbooks, support training, incident response, evidence, owner sign-offs, exception/waiver expiry, and proof that no legacy writes/credentials/paths remain.
Handle rollback without reintroducing unsafe endpoint DB trust or resurrecting removed credentials.
Define final deletion/retention/archive responsibilities and post-decommission monitoring.
cli: Automate read-only verification and residual monitoring
studies.gate: Final decommission requires zero unauthorized legacy writes, dispositioned buffers/consumers, revoked credentials, blocked paths, owned history, tested rollback, and multi-owner acceptance.
